speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with sudden-onset vertigo; to begin my assessment, have you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or tinnitus alongside the spinning sensation? Also, was the onset triggered by a specific head movement or position change?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The 3-minute duration, sudden onset during position change (going to bed), and lack of other neurologic deficits are classic for BPPV; I am requesting a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
